posts.text: 🇺🇦 Dutch and Austrian embassies in Kiev damaged during today's attack The buildings of the Dutch and Austrian embassies in Kiev were damaged during today's strikes, according to Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrey Sybiga. The photos show smashed windows in the Dutch embassy's guard post and broken glass and debris inside the Austrian embassy. Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said a projectile struck behind the embassy, causing minor damage, and that no staff were hurt. He didn't say what kind of projectile it was or who fired it, only that the Netherlands is "investigating exactly what happened." There are a few possible explanations. Falling debris from Ukrainian air defense interceptors regularly damages buildings in central Kiev. The strike may also have hit something next to the embassy rather than the embassy itself. The timing is awkward for The Hague either way. It comes days after Dutch arms maker Destinus boasted that its RUTA cruise missiles, about 700 of which the Dutch state is paying for, hit the Crimean Bridge two days in a row. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

☀️ This Thursday, November 19, marking 533 years since the Spanish colonization of the island, the organization Casa Pueblo protested in front of Castillo San Felipe del Morro to demand an immediate transition to solar energy and community control. ⚡️ Its executive director, Arturo Massol Deyá, linked the dependence on fossil fuels to the colonial condition of the country, called for lower electricity rates, took on LUMA and Genera PR, and wanted to stop the expansion of gas. 🌱 The day included actions in San Juan, Rincón, Fajardo, and New York to promote the Puerto Rico Pueblo Solar proposal and community microgrids against the centralized energy model.

📉 This Thursday, November 19, it was reported that, according to the Central Bank, Chile's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) fell by 1.1% year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026, and fixed investment dropped by 6.7%, contradicting the "investment boom" forecast by Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz. ⛏️ The report attributes the decline mainly to a 14.7% drop in mining and lower purchases of machinery, equipment, and engineering works, despite a 1.0% increase in non-mining GDP and higher consumption. 📊 The scenario occurs under the government of José Antonio Kast after a tax reform enacted in October and amid a situation that Quiroz himself has described as a technical recession.
